meta.title: Plaid Party · Watch together, in sync · PLAID
meta.description: Plaid Party, PLAID’s flagship feature, planned: one link, everyone on the same frame, each on the stream that suits their screen.

party.kicker: The intent is [written]({intent}); the spec isn’t.
party.title: Same film. Same second. Different couches.
party.lead: A Plaid Party keeps everyone on the same frame, wherever they are and whatever they watch on.

start.title: Start a party.
start.body: Pick a film, choose Plaid Party. You get a link and a short code to send.

joined.title: Everyone’s here.
joined.body: Friends join from a TV, a laptop or a phone. You see who’s watching and who’s still loading.

play.title: Press play once.
play.body: Play, pause and seek reach everyone together. The target: less than half a second between any two screens.

streams.title: 4K on the TV. 720p on the train.
streams.body: Everyone watches the same moment, but each device gets its own stream: Direct Play on the living room TV, a lighter transcode on a phone on mobile data. Nobody waits for the slowest connection.

drift.title: No “wait, where are you?”
drift.body: The server holds the clock. When someone drifts, PLAID nudges their speed instead of jumping. After buffering, they slide back in on their own.

pause.title: Sam asks for a pause.
pause.body: Anyone can ask. The host decides, or everyone does: your call.

reactions.name: Reactions
reactions.text: Emoji over the film, for everyone.

chat.name: Chat
chat.text: A side panel that never covers the picture.

pause.name: Pause requests
pause.text: A toast for the host, or for everyone.

control.name: Who controls
control.text: Host only, or everyone. Switch any time.

call.title: Credits.
call.body: Video and voice chat stay out of v1 on purpose. You probably already have a call open.

room.altToast: Concept of a Plaid Party room at 1:12:48, with a notice: Sam asks for a pause, Accept or Keep watching.

meta.title: PLAID · Your movies and shows, on your own server
meta.description: PLAID is a self-hosted, open-source media server: the films on your disks, streamed to every screen in the house. Watch alone, or together.

home.title: Your movies and shows, on your own server.
home.lead: PLAID indexes the films and series on your disks and streams them to every screen in the house. No central account, no subscription. Watch alone, or together.
home.state: **Early development.** The server, the web app and the Apple TV app work today. Sharing and Plaid Party are designed, not built. [Where we are]({roadmap}).

install18.title: One command, before anyone arrives.
install18.body: PLAID is a single Go binary with SQLite and FFmpeg. On Ubuntu or Debian, the script installs a system service that starts on boot. No Docker needed.
install18.note: amd64 or arm64: a Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 with a 64-bit OS is enough.

account.title: An account that lives on your server.
account.body: The first visit creates the admin account, on your machine. There’s no PLAID account online, and nothing to sign up for with us.

link.title: The link is sent.
link.body: Turn on remote access and your server gets an address with a real certificate. Friends open one link:
link.never: Your videos go straight from your server to them. getplaid.direct only answers DNS.

tv.title: On the TV, it’s an app.
tv.body: The Apple TV app finds the server on your network, pairs with a code, and plays with the same look and flow as the web. In English or French, per profile.

party.title: Everyone lands on the same frame.
party.body: Plaid Party is the feature PLAID is built around: one link, and play, pause and seek reach everyone at once, each on the stream that suits their screen. It’s designed, not built yet.

credits.title: Credits: two developers and a couch.
credits.body: PLAID is MIT licensed and built in the open. Every feature starts as a written intent, then a spec, then a plan, all on GitHub.

meta.title: Features · PLAID
meta.description: What PLAID does today and what comes next: libraries, artwork, Direct Play and transcoding, the web and Apple TV apps, remote access.

features.title: What works tonight, and what doesn’t yet.
features.lead: The basics, done on your hardware. Every line says where it stands.

scan.name: Folder scanning
scan.text: New files are picked up on their own; network shares are rescanned every 15 minutes. PLAID only reads your folders.

match.name: Matching and artwork
match.text: Titles, posters and synopses from TMDB and fanart.tv, in each library’s language. Your own `.nfo` files and images come first.

search.name: Search and collections
search.text: Find a film, a show or a person. Browse collections.

direct.name: Direct Play
direct.text: When a device can play the file as it is, PLAID sends it untouched. Almost no CPU.

transcode.name: Direct Stream and transcoding
transcode.text: When it can’t, PLAID remuxes or re-encodes to H.264 with FFmpeg, at a quality that fits the connection.

hw.name: Hardware transcoding
hw.text: VAAPI, Intel Quick Sync, NVENC or V4L2 M2M, tested at startup, with software as the fallback. [What works where]({hw}).

subs.name: Subtitles
subs.text: Text and image subtitles, with each profile’s audio and subtitle choices remembered.

resume.name: Continue watching
resume.text: Stop on the TV, pick up in the browser. Each profile keeps its place.

web.name: Web
web.text: Served by the server itself, in any recent browser.

appletv.name: Apple TV
appletv.text: A native tvOS app. It finds the server on the network and pairs with a code.

ios.name: iPhone and iPad
ios.text: Next in the Apple phase, in SwiftUI like the TV app.

android.name: Android and Android TV
android.text: Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, after the Apple apps.

accounts.name: Accounts and profiles
accounts.text: An admin, members, and a profile per person, with an optional PIN.

pairing.name: TV pairing
pairing.text: A TV signs in with a short code typed on another device.

remote.name: Remote access
remote.text: A getplaid.direct address and a real certificate for your server. [How it works]({remote}).

sharing.name: Library sharing
sharing.text: Invite a friend by link to one library or collection, with a quality cap and instant revocation.

statuses.title: What the labels mean
statuses.body: **Available**: merged and in the releases, still being polished. **Planned**: written as an intent, not built. **Later**: on the list, not designed yet.

meta.title: Install · PLAID
meta.description: Install PLAID on Ubuntu, Debian or Docker, on amd64 or arm64. Then open http://<your-server>:32500.

install.title: Install PLAID.
install.lead: Three ways, on Ubuntu, Debian or Docker. All of them end the same way: open `{url}`.

script.name: Script
script.body: Ubuntu or Debian. Installs a system service that starts on boot. No Docker needed.
script.note: It checks the package’s checksum before installing. [Read it first]({script}), it’s short.

service.what: Enabled and started, runs as the `plaid` user

docker.name: Docker
docker.body: Mount your media folders read-only in `docker-compose.yml`, then use the paths inside the container when you add a library.

open.title: Open it.
open.body: The first visit walks you through the admin account, your folders and their language.
open.note: Setup only works from your local network. From elsewhere, PLAID asks for the setup code it prints in its log.

folders.title: Point it at your folders.
folders.body: Movies and shows, each library in its own language. PLAID scans them, matches titles and fetches artwork. It never writes to your media.
folders.note: The native package runs PLAID as the `plaid` user, which can’t read your home folder by default. [Give it read access]({guide}).

systems.name: Systems
systems.value: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and 26.04 LTS, Debian 12 and later

arch.name: Architectures
arch.value: amd64 (most PCs), arm64 (Raspberry Pi 4 and 5 with a 64-bit OS, ARM servers)

everyday.body: Is it running, and what is it saying?

meta.title: Remote access · getplaid.direct · PLAID
meta.description: How PLAID’s built-in remote access works: a getplaid.direct address, a Let’s Encrypt certificate, and video that never passes through us.

remote.title: Your server, reachable from anywhere.
remote.lead: Turn it on in **Settings → Remote access**. Your server gets an address with a real certificate, and your videos never pass through us.

port.title: Open a port.
port.body: PLAID asks your router to open one with UPnP or NAT-PMP. If your router can’t, choose **Manual** and forward a TCP port to port `32501` of the PLAID machine.

name.title: Get a name.
name.body: PLAID registers with getplaid.direct, which points that name at your public IP and follows it when it changes. The server checks in every 15 minutes.

cert.title: Get a certificate.
cert.body: PLAID gets a Let’s Encrypt certificate for that name. The challenge goes through getplaid.direct’s DNS, so no port 80 is needed and the private key never leaves your server.

send.title: Send the link.
send.body: The short link redirects to your server, so friends only need one. Before you send it, getplaid.direct checks from outside that your server answers.

through.title: Video never goes through getplaid.direct
through.body: The link redirects once, DNS answers with your home IP, and from then on the device talks to your server directly. There is no relay: that's also why, behind CGNAT, you need a VPN like Tailscale instead.

video.route: From your server to your friend’s screen. Never through us.

dns.route: getplaid.direct answers DNS with your public IP.

cert.route: Let’s Encrypt checks a DNS record PLAID sets. The key stays home.

off.title: Turn it off.
off.body: Switch remote access off in the same settings: getplaid.direct deletes your server’s records at once. A server it hasn’t heard from in 30 days is removed too.

limits.title: When it can’t work

cgnat.name: Behind CGNAT
cgnat.text: Some fibre and mobile providers share one public IP between homes, so no port can be opened. Use a VPN such as Tailscale instead.

docker.name: In Docker
docker.text: UPnP can’t see your router from Docker’s default network. Use `network_mode: host`, or choose Manual and publish `32501:32501`.

own.name: Your own setup
own.text: Prefer your own domain, reverse proxy or tunnel? PLAID works behind them, with getplaid.direct left off. [Behind a reverse proxy]({proxy}).

limits.guide: Remote access in the install guide

meta.title: FAQ · PLAID
meta.description: Short answers about PLAID: price, what works today, your data, Raspberry Pi, Docker, and reaching your server from outside.

faq.title: Questions after the film.
faq.lead: Short answers. The install guide has the long ones.

free.a: Yes. It’s open source under the MIT license, with no paid tier.

today.a: Yes, early. The server, the web app and the Apple TV app work: libraries, artwork, playback, remote access. Sharing and Plaid Party come next. Expect rough edges, and check [the roadmap]({roadmap}).

fork.q: Is it a Plex or Jellyfin fork?
fork.a: No. PLAID is written from scratch, with its own API and its own apps.

account.q: Does PLAID need an online account?
account.a: No. Accounts live on your server. Nothing is required from us.

sends.q: Does it send anything to you?
sends.a: No telemetry. The server asks TMDB and fanart.tv for posters and synopses, sending titles, years and ids, never who watches what. With remote access on, getplaid.direct knows your public IP and port: [what it keeps]({privacy}).

files.a: Exactly where they were. PLAID reads your folders; it never moves or changes your media.

pi.q: Will it run on a Raspberry Pi?
pi.a: Yes, a Pi 4 or 5 with a 64-bit OS. Direct Play costs almost nothing. Transcoding on a Pi runs in software, so for files your devices can’t play as they are, a machine with a GPU helps. [Details]({hw}).

docker.a: No. The Debian package installs a regular system service. Docker works too.

outside.q: How do friends reach my server from outside?
outside.a: Turn on [remote access]({remote}): your server gets a getplaid.direct address and a real certificate, and video goes straight from you to them. Or use your own reverse proxy, or a tunnel like Tailscale or Cloudflare Tunnel: [the install guide covers it]({proxy}).

install.q: Do my friends need to install anything?
install.a: A browser is enough. On Apple TV, there’s an app.

meta.title: Privacy · PLAID
meta.description: What getplaid.direct stores about your server and for how long. The getplaid.tv website has no analytics and no cookies.

privacy.title: Privacy.
privacy.lead: What getplaid.direct keeps about your server, for how long, and what this website keeps about you: nothing.

stored.title: What getplaid.direct stores
stored.body: Only once you turn remote access on, and only this, per server:

items.slug: A name derived from your server’s name, like `living-room`
items.token: A hash (SHA-256) of the server’s secret token, never the token itself
items.ip: Your public IPv4 and IPv6 addresses
items.port: The external port your router forwards
items.seen: When the server registered and when it was last seen
items.acme: While a certificate is issued, temporary DNS challenge values, which expire after an hour

never.title: What it never sees
never.body: Your videos, your libraries, your accounts, or who watches what. Video goes straight from your server to the screen; getplaid.direct only answers DNS.

deleted.title: When it’s deleted
deleted.body: At once, when you turn remote access off. Automatically, when a server hasn’t been seen for 30 days.

server.title: The PLAID server itself
server.body: No telemetry. To match your films, it sends TMDB and fanart.tv their titles, years and ids, from your server’s IP. Nothing about your accounts or what anyone watches.

site.title: This website
site.body: No analytics, no cookies, no third-party scripts or fonts. If you switch to the light theme, that choice is stored in your browser only and never sent anywhere.

contact.title: Questions
contact.body: Open a [GitHub issue]({issues}). What the service does is specified in [its protocol]({protocol}).
